title: Budget Coverage for Contractual Commitments and Revenue Timing Guidance
author: Marta Alvarez
content:
Overview

This document describes the standard framework used by Redwood Inference finance, legal, sales, procurement, and FP&A teams to ensure that annual and multi-year budgets appropriately cover:

- Contractual commitments (discounts, minimum revenue guarantees, usage credits, free trials and onboarding credits).
- Sales concessions and procurement-driven refunds/credits.
- Timing differences that affect revenue recognition (deferred revenue, multi-element arrangements).

Purpose: provide a repeatable control process to quantify budget exposure from signed and in-flight contracts, drive forecasting consistency, and ensure appropriate accounting handoffs for revenue timing.

Scope

Applies to: all commercial contracts executed by Sales, channel partners, and procurement credit arrangements that create revenue concessions or material cost offsets. This includes Hosted API, Dedicated and Private contracts, and add-on observability/SLAs.

Thresholds (when the full process must be used):
1) Any commitment that alters list prices or creates credit/discount flows > $50k ARR impact -> full coverage analysis required.
2) Deals with multi-year non-cancellable commitments where the committed spend crosses 12+ months -> include forecast-level revenue timing review.
3) Any bespoke procurement or vendor credit agreement > $100k total value -> involve finance and legal.

Definitions

- Budget Coverage Amount: the incremental budget (or reallocation) required to offset the net impact of a contractual concession over the budget horizon.
- Contractual Exposure: present value of discounts/credits/guarantees embedded in a contract.
- Revenue Timing Delta: difference between cash/billing schedule and recognized revenue as governed by ASC 606 / local GAAP.

Roles and Ownership

- Sales: raise Contract Intake (Confluence link + SFDC opportunity ID), provide modeled pricing schedule, and mark expected billing cadence.
- Legal: review contract for concessions, termination rights, and any change in deliverables that affect revenue allocation.
- FP&A (owner of budget coverage analysis): calculate Budget Coverage Amount, update operating plan, and propose budget action (reallocate, reserve, or request incremental budget).
- RevRec / Accounting: determine revenue timing and appropriate deferrals; provide journal entry templates.
- Procurement: track vendor credits/offsets that affect cost of goods sold (COGS) or operating expense and notify FP&A for budget alignment.

Budget Coverage Requirements (step-by-step)

1) Contract Intake and Tagging (Sales)
   - Log contract in SFDC within 48 hours of offer acceptance. Tag with labels: "budget-impact", "revrec-review" if it contains discounts/credits/usage guarantees.
   - Upload final signed contract to the contract repository and notify Legal and FP&A.

2) Initial Exposure Quantification (FP&A within 5 business days)
   - Model: create a 36-month cash and recognition model using official pricing schedule. Use conservative consumption assumptions (baseline, target, upside).
   - Deliverable: single-sheet "Budget Coverage Summary" with columns: Period, Billings (cash), Forecasted Recognized Revenue, Gross Impact (discount/credit), Net Budget Coverage Required.

3) Legal and RevRec Alignment (concurrent)
   - Legal annotates contract clauses that create performance obligations or billing exceptions.
   - RevRec determines whether credits/discounts are a standalone performance obligation or a price concession impacting transaction price. Document the accounting conclusion.

4) FP&A Recommendation and Budget Action (within 10 business days)
   - Options: (a) Absorb within existing route/segment budget if impact < 2% of segment budget; (b) Create a reserve (P&L contra) for expected concession; (c) Request an incremental budget reallocation from Finance leadership.
   - Decision logged to the Opportunity record with approver signatures (email + Confluence approval entry).

5) Monthly Monitoring
   - Add contract to FP&A watchlist if Budget Coverage Amount > $25k. Update recognized vs. budgeted variance weekly for the first 90 days, then monthly for the remainder of the contract.

Contract Review Checklist (for Legal + Finance)

1) Identify all monetary concessions: percent discounts, credit lines, free service periods, onboarding credits.
2) Confirm billing cadence and invoicing triggers.
3) Cross-reference SLA credits and penalty schedules — quantify worst-case exposure.
4) Flag change-of-control, assignment, and termination terms that could accelerate revenue recognition or create refunds.
5) If the contract contains reseller/channel carve-outs, confirm who is legally the seller of record.

Template table: Contract Financial Snapshot

| Field | Example/Instructions |
|-------|----------------------|
| Opportunity ID | SFDC-2025-10123 |
| Customer | Acme Video Inc. |
| Contract Start / End | 2026-04-01 / 2028-03-31 |
| Total Contracted Value (TCV) | $1,200,000 |
| Upfront Payment | $200,000 |
| Recurring Billings | $1,000,000 over 24 months |
| Identified Credits/Discounts | $120,000 (10% volume discount) |
| Budget Coverage Amount | $100,000 (FP&A computed) |
| RevRec Timing Flag | Multi-element; deferral required |

Revenue Recognition Interaction and Typical Accounting Treatment

- Price concessions that are expected to be offered at contract signing: reduce transaction price and flow through revenue as a reduction to recognized revenue over the related performance period.
- Usage credits that are refundable or transferrable: treated as a liability (deferred revenue or contract liability) until consumed.
- SLA credits (penalties): record as a liability reserve when the obligation arises; estimate probability and expected amount.

Simple example journal entry (YAML-style snippet for the accounting system template):

```
- period: 2026-04
  entries:
    - account: AccountsReceivable
      debit: 200000
    - account: UnearnedRevenue
      credit: 200000
    - account: Revenue
      credit: 0 # recognized later
    - account: RevenueReserve_SLA
      credit: 0 # adjusted when SLA credit granted
```

And an example of reducing recognized revenue for an agreed 10% committed discount over 12 months: 

```
# recognition schedule (monthly)
monthly_reduction = (TCV * 0.10) / 12
```

Forecasting Controls and Metrics

- Budget Coverage Ratio (BCR) = (Budget Coverage Amount) / (Segment Annual Budget). Target control threshold: BCR <= 0.02 (2%) to be considered immaterial; otherwise route to executive approval.
- Realized vs. Modeled Delta: track the difference between modeled usage and actuals; if > 15% for three consecutive months, trigger forecast rebase.
- Reserve Utilization Rate: track usage of previously created reserves; target utilization < 75% to avoid chronic under-provisioning.

Operational Procedures (people & systems)

- System tags: opportunities must include SFDC custom fields: budget_impact_flag (Y/N), contract_accounting_flag (revrec_hold/ready).
- Confluence: each Budget Coverage analysis must be attached to the Opportunity page and include an FP&A sign-off line.
- Monthly Close: RevRec posts adjustments no later than the 7th business day of the month with supporting Contract Financial Snapshot.

Escalation and Exceptions

- If Sales or Legal seeks to accept a concession that will increase BCR > 5% without an offset, they must obtain written approval from the VP Finance and the Head of Sales.
- For exceptions required by strategic deals, document the strategic rationale, expected lifetime value uplift, and a 12-month re-evaluation plan.

Templates and Appendix

- Budget Coverage Summary (sample header):
  - Opportunity ID, Customer, FP&A Analyst, Date, Modeled Scenarios (Conservative / Base / Upside), Budget Coverage Amount by year.

- Contract Credit Allowance Matrix (example):
  - Onboarding credit <= $25k: absorb in segment budget; > $25k and <= $50k: FP&A reserve recommended; > $50k: executive approval required.

Questions and next steps

If you are a partner with a high-value channel arrangement or expect a deal that will create material budget exposure, engage FP&A and Legal during the commercial stage (prior to signature). Use the SFDC tags and attach the Budget Coverage Summary to avoid month-end surprises.
